newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn passes investment incentives for east states.
newsitem.headline: Bonn passes investment incentives for east states.

text.p: The upper house of Germany's parliament on Friday approved continued transfers of about 5.7 billion marks ($3.3 billion) annually in investment incentives to the formerly communist eastern states and west Berlin until 2004.
Starting next year, however, the incentives will take the form of payments rather than the former tax credits, which were harder to audit.

The bill "creates the conditions for a long-term, sustainable reconstruction of the east," economics minister Guenter Rexrodt said. "Criticism from the west is misplaced. These funds are well invested in the future of our country."

Saxony premier Kurt Biedenkopf welcomed the vote, saying it sent the right signal at the right time. Earlier this week, some parliamentarians from the east warned that Finance Minister Theo Waigel was planning sharp cuts in aid to the east as part of his effort to trim the federal budget deficit.
The bill provides for government payments of 10 to 20 percent for capital investments.
-- Terence Gallagher, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097150 ($ = 1.751 German Marks)
